newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN POLICE COMPUTER TENDERS SCRUTINISED.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN POLICE COMPUTER TENDERS SCRUTINISED.

text.p: South African Auditor-General Henri Kleuver's office is investigating alleged irregularities in tender procedures involving contracts worth millions of rands for police computer systems since 1986.

Corporate executive manager Wally van Heerden told Reuters on Thursday the investigation was being conducted at the request of Police Commissioner George Fivaz and was expected to be completed within weeks.
"Various allegations have been made regarding the process that was followed and tender specifications for one tender in January this year, and about the fairness of the tender," he said.
"We are conducting a forensic audit that covers systems development as well as a regulatory audit."

This meant that although only one specific tender, RT 9963, had been singled out because of the allegations, the investigation also covered contracts awarded in the development of the police's information technology systems since the mid-1980s.
The investigation was started in February and outside expertise was contracted in to help audit staff.

A statement released by Kleuver's office said the investigation would review the management of "relevant business risks as well as the controls over and effectiveness of the tender procedures currently in place, but will not necessarily be limited to specific contracts of, or suppliers to, the South African Police Service."
It added that the allegations made had not yet been substantiated.
